name: APT28
notes: Russian GRU unit. Focuses on espionage and data exfiltration. Known for credential harvesting and lateral movement through enterprise networks.

name: APT29
notes: Russian SVR unit. Highly sophisticated supply-chain compromise specialist. Responsible for SolarWinds SUNBURST. Patient, long-dwell intrusions.

name: Lazarus Group
notes: North Korean state-sponsored group. Primarily motivated by financial theft (SWIFT heists, crypto exchanges) and espionage. Deploys ransomware and wipers.

name: Turla
notes: Russian FSB. Exceptional stealth and persistence. Known for using compromised satellite links as C2. Long-term cyber espionage operations.

name: HAFNIUM
notes: Chinese state-sponsored. Exploited ProxyLogon/ProxyShell Exchange vulnerabilities at scale. Targets US-based entities for intelligence collection.

name: APT41
notes: Chinese state-sponsored with a dual mandate — espionage and financial crime. Rapid exploitation of newly disclosed CVEs. Prolific and versatile.

name: APT32
notes: Vietnamese state-sponsored. Targets regional neighbors and dissidents. Sophisticated spear-phishing and watering-hole campaigns.

name: Sandworm Team
notes: Russian GRU Unit 74455. Responsible for NotPetya and Ukraine power grid attacks. Specialises in destructive operations against critical infrastructure.

name: Wizard Spider
notes: Russian financially motivated group. Operates TrickBot, Conti, and Ryuk ransomware. Targets high-value victims via initial access brokers.

name: Volt Typhoon
notes: Chinese state-sponsored. Pre-positions in US critical infrastructure for potential disruption. Uses living-off-the-land techniques and compromised SOHO devices as proxies.

name: Scattered Spider
notes: English-speaking financially motivated group. Masters of social engineering and MFA bypass. Responsible for MGM and Caesars attacks.

name: APT38
notes: North Korean financial operations arm of Lazarus. Specialises in SWIFT heists and banking system intrusions. Deployes destructive malware post-exfiltration.

name: APT33
notes: Iranian state-sponsored. Targets aviation and energy sectors. Deploys Shamoon and other destructive malware. Also operates ransomware campaigns.

name: APT1
notes: Chinese PLA Unit 61398. Large-scale, systematic IP theft from US companies. Focused on 20 strategic industries. Known for years-long persistent access.

name: Gamaredon Group
notes: Russian FSB unit targeting Ukraine. High volume, lower sophistication. Persistent spear-phishing and USB-based malware distribution.

name: INDRIK SPIDER
notes: Russian financially motivated group under OFAC sanctions. Operates BitPaymer, WastedLocker, Hades ransomware. Recently targeting critical infrastructure.

name: Rocke Group
notes: Chinese-speaking cryptomining and cloud-targeting group. Exploits publicly exposed services and container escapes. Deploys rootkits to hide mining activity.

name: TeamTNT
notes: Specialises in cloud and container exploitation for cryptomining and credential theft. Targets exposed Docker APIs and Kubernetes clusters.

name: Tortoiseshell
notes: Iranian state-sponsored. Targets IT service providers to reach downstream victims (supply-chain). Uses fake social media profiles for initial access.

name: FIN7
notes: Financially motivated Eastern European group. Pioneered CARBANAK malware for banking fraud. Evolved to ransomware (REVIL, BlackMatter) and data extortion.
